extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, petitioners (third parties), and patent owners
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the USPTO Board trial (Inter Partes Review) standards and procedural requirements for challenging the patentability of claims under §§102 and 103, including who may file, timing, institution standard, and decision timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of review (grounds and subject matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes review is a trial proceeding ... to review the patentability of one or more claims in a patent only on a ground that could be raised under §§ 102 or 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proceeding is limited to patentability challenges under 35 U.S.C. §§102 (novelty) and 103 (obviousness); other statutory grounds are not available in IPR. The review is of one or more claims (not other patent issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art basis limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Review is only on the basis of prior art consisting of patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only patents and printed publications may be used as prior art in an IPR petition; other types of prior art (e.g., prior public uses not captured in patents/printed publications) are not proper grounds for IPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes review process begins with a third party (a person who is not the owner of the patent) filing a petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only non-owners (third parties) may file petitions to institute IPR. Patent owners cannot initiate IPR against their own patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing petitions (first-inventor-to-file patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: For first-inventor-to-file patents, inter partes review process begins with a third party filing a petition after the later of either: (1) 9 months after the grant of the patent or issuance of a reissue patent; or (2) if a post grant review is instituted, the termination of the post grant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions for first-inventor-to-file patents are subject to these timing restrictions; these deadlines do not apply to first-to-invent patents. Practitioners must calculate the 'later of' date to determine petitionability. If a post grant review is instituted, IPR timing is deferred until that PGR terminates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner preliminary response
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may file a preliminary response to the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners have the option to file a preliminary response addressing the petition's arguments and evidence prior to the Board's institution decision. The preliminary response can be used to explain why institution is not warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An inter partes review may be instituted upon a showing that there is a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail with respect to at least one claim challenged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board uses the 'reasonable likelihood' standard (i.e., reasonable likelihood to prevail on at least one challenged claim) when deciding whether to institute IPR. Petition drafting should therefore focus on demonstrating that likelihood for at least one claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision/timeline for final determination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proceeding is instituted and not dismissed, a final determination by the Board will be issued within 1 year (extendable for good cause by 6 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board aims to issue a final written decision within one year of institution; that period may be extended for good cause by up to six months. Parties should plan discovery, motions, and hearings with these time constraints in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure for conducting inter partes review took effect on September 16, 2012, and applies to any patent issued before, on, or after September 16, 2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR procedures apply retroactively to patents issued before the effective date as well as those issued on or after that date. Practitioners should be aware of the procedural regime's start date when assessing challenges to older patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritative statutory and regulatory references
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 USC Ch. 31 §311 - §319; Inter Partes Review Rules (37 CFR Ch. 42, Subpart B); Inter Partes Review FAQs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal authority for IPR requirements and procedures resides in 35 U.S.C. Ch. 31 (sections 311–319) and the rules at 37 C.F.R. Part 42 Subpart B; practitioners should consult these statutes/regulations and the USPTO FAQs for detailed procedural and filing requirements. Search and case-tracking are available via P-TACTS and related USPTO pages.
